svg.title: How a scan on the phone reaches Paperless
svg.desc: On the phone, the scanner of the Nextcloud app saves the pages as a PDF into the folder Inbox, or the auto upload of the app takes a file from a folder of the phone into it. With the next run of Paperless Sync, at the interval that the administrator set, 5 minutes by default, the file goes to Paperless, which reads its text and makes it a document. When Paperless imports it, the file leaves the inbox, and the next run writes the copy of the new document into the archive, in the folders of its correspondent, its type and its year, with the marker of its ID, such as [P123], in its name; the phone finds it there. When the import fails, such as for a document that Paperless has already, the file moves to the folder Failed imports, next to a .error.txt that gives the reason; a file that Paperless refuses at once, such as one of a type that it doesn't take, stays in the inbox until it changes. Your steps are orange, Nextcloud blue, Paperless-ngx green and a failed import red.
